top.abstract: Abstract Introduction: Detrimental effects of inadequate sleep on athletic performance have been well documented. Increasing sleep (sleep extension) has not been thoroughly investigated, especially among college athletes whose student status makes them particularly vulnerable to sleep restriction. Furthermore, the effects of sleep on an athlete’s nutrition behaviors have yet to be determined. top.title: From Purification to Protection: Plague Response in Late Medieval Valencia
top.abstract: On the morning of 6 July 1395, the city council of Valencia met in the council chamber. Plague had been in the city since March, and despite the council's best efforts, the death toll continued to rise. This morning, the councilmen authorized several new measures to combat the epidemic. They organized charitable donations "to placate divine anger," and a procession to the chapel of Our Lady of Mercy to "beseech divine mercy for the said plague." top.title: Encountering the Plague: Old Testament Insights into the Pastoral Literature of Luther, Calvin, and Beza
top.abstract: The Black Death that devastated much of the medieval world beginning in the 14th century continued to take its toll during the Protestant Reformation era in the 15th century. This article examines the pastoral letters of three Protestant Reformers whose theological responses to the plight of the pestilence come to the fore, especially in their use of the Old Testament in their writings: Whether One May Flee from a Deadly Plague (1527) by Martin Luther, To Monsieur le Curé de Cernex (1543) by John Calvin, and A Learned Treatise of the Plague (1579) by Theodore Beza.
